pundit.name: Landon Donovan
pundit.take: **Look, I get why people say Norway is an emerging team, but when your manager is “Ghost Pepper” Devin, you have to wonder if he’s just picking teams based on their flag colors.** I truly feel for Devin, bless his heart, running such a valiant race in second place with 71 points. But when you draft Haiti and they end up being a conversation-stopping anchor on your roster, you have to question the strategy. His recent match with Spain against Belgium showed flashes of brilliance, elevating his stock by 13 points, but it also underscores that Devin's relying on Spain to keep him afloat. Meanwhile, “The Backpass Assassin” Gayden has bizarrely opted for a roster featuring the likes of Japan and Ivory Coast alongside the formidable England, suggesting he picks teams with the fervor of someone choosing their favorite figures in a Madden game. One can only assume he's banking on England to storm through the group stage—an assumption as shaky as hoping for an early English summer. In the impending Norway vs. England clash, Devin's team spirit might just bring him joy, but I have the utmost misplaced confidence in Gayden's England squad to come out on top, possibly simply by being the least confused on the field.
